card.name: Words just before explanatory or mechanism terms
card.fires_on: Small connecting or modifying words that come right before a noun or verb about explaining a cause or mechanism. Examples are 'because', 'via', 'active' before 'metabolite', and 'simply' before 'pushes'.

modes.label: Active before metabolite
modes.description: The word 'active' after 'its' or 'the pharmacologically', right before 'metabolite(s)' in drug interaction text.
modes.example: Digoxin had no effects on the pharmacokinetics of nefazodone and its<< active>> metabolites.

modes.label: Reasoning connectors
modes.description: Words like 'because', 'via' or 'simply' that introduce a reason or mechanism in prose.
modes.example: If you don't actually know why the sky is blue, don't just say '<<because>> God made it that way.'

modes.label: Explain verb
modes.description: The verb 'explain' in a sentence about what a finding could account for.
